context_requirements: Active transcription and proliferation (RNAP II dependence)
Intact apoptotic machinery for late cell death
TP53 status modulates the late arm (wild-type lines favor CDKN1A/GADD45 induction)
falsifiers: No decrease in proliferation-associated landmark transcripts (e.g., MYC, CCNA2, CCNB1) at 24 h in any line
No induction of immediate-early genes (FOS, JUN, EGR1) at 6 h
Responses indistinguishable from vehicle across all nine lines
Selective strong response in only one line with no dose- or time-dependence

evidence.supports: 3'-ethynylcytidine, an RNA polymerase inhibitor, inhibits transcription and sensitizes tumor cells, supporting antiproliferative transcriptional consequences in human cancer lines
RNAP inhibitors block nucleotide addition, establishing direct inhibition of transcription as the mechanism
RNAP switch-region inhibitors block transcriptional initiation, supporting rapid loss of RNA synthesis

changes: Removed TRIB3 from proximal_up: TRIB3 is a stress/ATF4 target, not an immediate-early RNAP-II-inhibition response; it remains in late_up.
Removed TRIB3 from late_up duplicate? No: kept once in late_up and removed from proximal_up to avoid duplication across time points.
Kept POLR2I/POLR2K/POLR1C in proximal_down: RNAP subunit genes are transcriptionally downregulated under RNAP inhibition.
Kept MYC/CCND1 in proximal_down and MYC/CCNA2/CCNB1/CDK1 etc. in late_down: consistent with loss of RNA synthesis and proliferation.
Kept immediate-early genes FOS/JUN/EGR1/ZFP36/IER3/NFKBIA/NFKBIB/NFKBIE/TNIP1/DUSP4/DUSP6 in proximal_up: stress-responsive genes can be transiently induced by transcriptional stress.
Kept CDKN1A/GADD45A/GADD45B/DDIT4/SESN1/TSC22D3/SQSTM1/HERPUD1/XBP1/DNAJB1/HSPA1A/HSPB1/BAG3/CHAC1 in late_up: consistent with p53-dependent arrest, stress, and UPR at 24 h.
Kept line_response as given: no line-specific contradiction with known lineage/driver status was identified from the provided information.
Kept kinetics fast and magnitude moderate/strong: consistent with rapid RNAP inhibition and progressive transcriptional collapse.
Kept evidence PMIDs 25087851, 14576436, 21477256: abstracts support RNAP inhibition and antiproliferative/transcriptional consequences.
